parakeet: That's not research. That's your brain auto-completing the answer that you already wanted. I remember talking with a friend who was sure their belief was bulletproof. They typed in evidenced against X, but only clicked on the articles that ended up backing X. Now, when I called them out, they swore they'd looked into it and they literally had for three minutes and 15 seconds. That's confirmation bias, the silent filter that drowns out every doubter. In your journal or notes app, write down one belief you've only ever searched to support. Then, and this is the key, hunt down one solid statistic or peer-reviewed study that challenges it. No excuses. You're mining for truth, not comfort. Breaking this filter is the first step toward genuine openness because if you never see the evidence that contradicts you, you'll never have to question yourself or evolve. And please keep in mind that I said evidence, not anecdote. The plural of anecdote is not data.
